rename.resolution: re-verdicted `declined` -- the rename's only argument was rust:ParameterKind, which is itself declined; the method is named after the type we keep

why: RE-VERDICTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), was `rename`. rclrs names the trait method that reports a variant's type `kind()`, returning `ParameterKind`; ours is `parameter_type()`, returning `ParameterType` (both are associated fns with no receiver -- ours at `packages/core/nros-params/src/types.rs:426`). The rename justified itself entirely by pointing at `rust:ParameterKind` -- whose verdict is `declined`, because ours is the better name of the two: it is what `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterType`, rclcpp and our own C (`nros_parameter_type_t`) all call it. The stated reason therefore resolves AGAINST the rename. Renaming the method alone would buy no rclrs parity either -- a `kind()` that returns a `ParameterType` still does not match rclrs's `kind() -> ParameterKind` -- while costing the one consistency we do have, that the accessor is named for the type it returns. What a user loses: the `kind()` spelling. Ours half: `rust:ParameterVariant::parameter_type`.
